learning_outcomes.text: Student knows and understands basic concepts, subject, and tasks of ergonomics.
Student has up-to-date knowledge on basic legal acts concerning occupational safety in electrical power engineering.

Student knows basic legal acts concerning occupational safety in electrical power engineering; characteristics of legal acts: Council Directives no. 89/391, Constitution of the Republic of Poland, Labor Code.
Student knows basic concepts, causes of accidents and occupational diseases, benefits for accidents at work and occupational diseases.

Student knows what company OHS policy is; the importance of costs in OHS policy; certificates for OHS MS. Methods of occupational risk assessment; hazard vs. risk; risk at workplaces; occupational risk assessment.

syllabus_topics: Safety of electrical device use: LECTURES: 1. Ergonomics and related issues: Environmental factors in the workplace of greatest importance in electrical power engineering; characteristics of selected dangerous, harmful, and onerous factors. Impact of electromagnetic fields: natural electromagnetic fields and those from technical devices as a factor threatening human health; Noise; basic concepts; noise intensity; types of noise; permissible noise values; prevention. Industrial dusts in the workplace; impact of dusts on the human body; protection against excessive dusting; prevention.
2. Basic legal acts concerning occupational safety in electrical power engineering: characteristics of legal acts.
3. Accidents and occupational diseases: basic concepts, causes of accidents and occupational diseases, benefits for accidents at work and occupational diseases.

4. Impact of electric current on the human body: electric shocks when operating electrical devices; types and conditions of impacts; limit current intensity values. Principles of conduct in case of electric shock; freeing the shocked person from current; assessment of the shocked person's condition; types of first aid provided. Scope of first aid provided to the shocked person; artificial respiration and indirect heart massage; description and principles of selecting individual artificial respiration methods; conduct in case of one or two rescuers; control of effectiveness and conduct in case of restoration of breathing and circulation.

5. Basic and additional shock protection: methods of implementing protection against direct contact; methods of implementing protection against indirect contact: fast shutdown (examples), equipotential bonding, protection class II, workplace isolation, electrical separation; simultaneous protection. Voltages in shock protection; operating, touch, step, shock, safe voltage; technical methods of implementing safe voltages; types of network systems.

6. Occupational safety and health management systems; company OHS policy; importance of costs in OHS policy; certificates for OHS MS. Methods of occupational risk assessment; hazard vs. risk; risk at workplaces; occupational risk assessment.
assessment_rules: Learning outcomes are verified by a test and a presentation. Active participation in the lecture is a condition for crediting.
